subject: [ACME] Coordinating AWS Private Offer — approval tiers and term options

Subject: AWS private offer — confirmation of approval lanes and term length

Hi Jasmine / Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the technical team was impressed with the latency profiles on the GenLarge models. Procurement asked me to confirm a few things before we escalate to our legal/approvals team:

- Can Redwood provide a 12 month vs 24 month pricing comparison for the private offer (list + proposed discount)?
- For AWS Private Offer routing, which buyer approval tiers should we expect for a >$250k ARR commitment? Any seller-guided steps to speed approvals?
- If we propose a 12-month term with an annual true-up, will Redwood accept a PO-style payment (Net 30) or do you require upfront commitment?

I've attached the PO template our legal team prefers (see attachment). We can also run a joint call with our procurement lead if that helps — they are available Wed/Thu next week PST.

Appreciate a short summary we can drop into our procurement packet.

Best,
Tom
Tom Briggs
Head of IT Procurement | AcmeHealth

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — confirmation of approval lanes and term length

Tom — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below and then a suggested next step.

1) Pricing by term: we can do both 12- and 24-month constructs. Attached is a two-column summary (annualized list + proposed reseller discount band). For a commit in the $250k+ range we typically surface a 15-22% discount vs list depending on annual vs usage mix.

2) Buyer approval tiers on AWS Marketplace: for private offers above $200k, buyers usually need a procurement signoff plus a cloud-finance approval. Seller-guided private offers can speed routing if we use the AWS Marketplace Private Offer APIs and include our co-sell registration. We typically include a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) that clarifies responsibilities and required approvers which shortens procurement back-and-forth.

3) Payment terms: Redwood accepts Net 30 on PO for agreements executed via AWS private offer, provided the PO references the executed private offer and the billing contact is set in the AWS Marketplace record. Upfront pre-pay is optional for certain enterprise packs but not required.

Suggested next step: I'll put together a concise MAP + a clean private-offer attachment that your procurement/legal can drop into the packet. Can we schedule a 30-min sync on Wednesday 25 May at 10am PT? If that works I'll invite our legal ops (Marissa) and kathy@aws-partner (optional) to join.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Tom — adding the two items inline before the sync.

1) Escalation contact for SLA exceptions: Primary — Marissa Cole, Head of Customer Success (marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com; +1 415-555-0199). Secondary — Karthik Iyer, Director Partnerships (karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com). We will include these in the MAP and the private offer notes so your procurement team sees a clear owner.

2) Audit clause: we can accept a standard customer audit clause with two caveats: (a) audits are limited to data related to the AcmeHealth account and (b) we require reasonable notice (30 days) and mutual NDA/POA for any on-prem review. If you can paste the exact clause we'll flag anything unusual; most templates are fine and we can accommodate via an addendum.

Attached is a cleaned one-page MAP and the private-offer summary Jasmine referenced. We'll review during the call and get you a final pricing table that maps to 12- vs 24-month economics.

Cheers,
Marissa
